articles.title: How to Find and Replace Data in Excel with Python and Highlight Matches
articles.excerpt: Reports exported from several systems rarely use the same wording. One file says "North America", another says "America"; a department was renamed last quarter; a column header oscillates between "Tot…
articles.body: Reports exported from several systems rarely use the same wording. One file says "North America", another says "America"; a department was renamed last quarter; a column header oscillates between "Total" and "Sum". Fixing this by hand has a second, quieter cost: after the edits nobody knows which cells were touched, so verification becomes a line-by-line comparison. A more practical approach is to let a script perform the replacement and color every changed cell at the same time, so the affected area is visible at a glance. In Python this can be done with Spire.XLS for Python. Beyond plain string replacement, the library supports regular expression matching, numeric and formula lookup, and replacement that applies a new style in the same call, which covers most report-cleaning scenarios.
articles.author: Allen Yang

articles.title: The Silent Killers of AI Code: How "Vibe Coding" is Rotting Codebases from the Inside
articles.excerpt: We have officially entered the era of "vibe coding". You type a prompt into Cursor or Claude Code, watch hundreds of lines of polished TypeScript or Python scroll past, eye the green test suite, and h…
articles.body: We have officially entered the era of "vibe coding". You type a prompt into Cursor or Claude Code, watch hundreds of lines of polished TypeScript or Python scroll past, eye the green test suite, and hit merge. Engineering velocity has never looked higher on paper. Features that once took weeks now take hours, and product managers are celebrating unprecedented delivery metrics. But behind the shiny dashboard numbers, senior architects and core maintainers are starting to sound an alarm. A silent, structural decay is creeping into modern software repositories: Synthetic Code Rot. It isn't obvious at first. The tests pass, the linter doesn't complain, and the code compiles without warnings.
articles.author: Saranyo Deyasi

articles.title: Exploring End-to-End Test Automation: More Than Just Execution
articles.excerpt: When we talk about test automation, the first thing that often comes to mind is writing scripts and running tests. But is test automation really just about that? As I've been exploring this field, I'v…
articles.body: When we talk about test automation, the first thing that often comes to mind is writing scripts and running tests. But is test automation really just about that? As I've been exploring this field, I've started looking at testing from a broader perspective. Writing a test is one part of the process. Understanding what to test, making sure the test is reliable, investigating failures, and keeping tests useful as an application changes are equally important. In this post, I want to share some of my thoughts on end-to-end test automation, how AI is becoming part of it, and what I'm interested in learning more about. What Is End-to-End Test Automation? Imagine you're using an online shopping application.

articles.title: Firefox Passkeys: How They Work and How to Use Them
articles.excerpt: Passkeys are a replacement for passwords using public-key cryptography. Firefox 122+ has built-in passkey support. Here's how it works and how to use it. A passkey is a pair of cryptographic keys: Pri…
articles.body: Passkeys are a replacement for passwords using public-key cryptography. Firefox 122+ has built-in passkey support. Here's how it works and how to use it. What Passkeys Are A passkey is a pair of cryptographic keys: Private key : Stored on your device (in a secure enclave or hardware security key), never leaves the device Public key : Stored on the website When you sign in, the website sends a challenge. Your device proves it has the private key by signing the challenge, without ever sending the key itself. No password is transmitted.

articles.title: I Built a Free Cargo Line Planner for Transport Fever 3

articles.body: Transport Fever 3 changed the one thing every transport sim player takes for granted: cargo no longer has a destination. In Transport Fever 2, an industry produced goods "for" a town and your job was connecting the dots. In TF3, cargo just sits at the industry until one of your lines collects it. Nothing moves unless you move it. That single design change turns fleet sizing from arithmetic into guesswork — how many vehicles does a line actually need when there's no demand signal telling you? I kept getting it wrong in my own games. So I built a small free tool to do the math: the Transport Fever 3 Cargo Line Planner ( https://gametinkerer.com/transport-fever-3/cargo-line-planner/ ). What it does (three things, nothing more) 1. Size a line.

articles.body: Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is one of the most significant recent privacy improvements to how HTTPS works. Firefox 118+ supports it. Here's what it does and why it matters. The Problem ECH Solves When you connect to a website over HTTPS, the TLS handshake reveals more than you might think. Specifically, the Server Name Indication (SNI) — the hostname you're connecting to — is sent in plaintext during the initial handshake, before encryption kicks in.

Even when I can’t mount my phone to my car dashboard, I use its audio navigation to guide me to destinations I’m not familiar with. But as the app has rolled out newer features, I’ve had a habit of ignoring them. My You tab remains neglected, and I’ve only ever left two reviews (both seven years ago) in the app. I also happily ignore the recommendations that appear when I’m about to search for something. Interview with the Vampire is a messy, queer love story, with an unreliable narrator sharing centuries of relationship drama. Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil provides three unreliable narrators who all lie to themselves and each other as their stories intertwine across the centuries. Schwab conceals their motivations and key parts of their history to tease the reader as she jumps back and forth in time, introducing the effects of a character’s mistake long before the cause becomes clear.

articles.title: It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say
articles.excerpt: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system based on the Milky Way's gravity, including its dark matter.
articles.body: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier. That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University. The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun , they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars.

articles.body: Fantasy is a broad genre of fiction, and low fantasy might be one of its most slippery corners. Unlike high fantasy, which often transports readers to entirely invented worlds with their own mythologies, low fantasy finds the extraordinary lurking just beneath the surface of the familiar.

articles.excerpt: Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was known for its visual humor, but this is the best-ever quote from the series
articles.body: Larson didn’t do deep . He didn’t do inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful in the lofty sense. They required thought because Larson’s work was brilliant, and you sometimes had to figure out what the punchline was. For example, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly on his glasses. Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

articles.body: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. articles.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
articles.excerpt: The incident is likely 1st confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered by targeted ads.
articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.
articles.author: Dan Goodin

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.
articles.author: Robert Lea

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.
